objectives.understand: Why AI needs one real, accepted example to reproduce your workplace's format.
objectives.do: Use the format-following prompt and the template-extraction prompt on a document you write often.
objectives.demonstrate: Choose the right example to supply, read a prompt for missing safeguards, and match tone to the reader.
objectives.apply: Save one template and draft one real document you owe someone this week.

discover.title: Mission briefing: the memo that came back
discover.scenario: Mr Adeyemi's memo came back from the Director's office covered in red ink: wrong heading block, no reference number, and 'Dear Sir' where the ministry writes 'The Director'. The AI had written a good memo, but not in his ministry's format. Today you teach AI your office's exact format once, and reuse it.

keyIdeas: Don't ask for 'a memo'. Paste one old, accepted example and tell the AI to follow its exact structure.
The template-extraction prompt turns any good document into a fill-in template you reuse.
One line switches the tone: more official, more concise or more warm.

missions.title: Pick the example to paste
missions.scenario: You need to write a quarterly activity report for your NGO's programme officer, in your organisation's format.
missions.prompt: Which example should you paste into the format-following prompt?

options.text: A sample activity report template you found online.
options.feedback: It will follow someone else's format, which is exactly the mistake today's lesson warns about.

options.text: Last quarter's report, which your programme officer accepted without corrections.
options.feedback: Yes. It carries your organisation's real headings, order and house style, and you know it was accepted.

options.text: Your draft from last week, which is still waiting for review.
options.feedback: It might still need corrections, so you could be teaching the AI your mistakes.

options.text: No example. Describe the format in words instead.
options.feedback: That helps a little, but a real example carries far more detail than you can describe.

missions.hint: The lesson is specific about which old document to use.
missions.support: You want the AI to copy a document that someone in authority has already approved. Which option is the accepted one from your own workplace?
missions.explain: One accepted example from your own workplace carries the format, vocabulary and house style that would take you paragraphs to describe. It is also known to be correct.

missions.title: Match the tone to the reader
missions.scenario: The same update needs to go to different people.
missions.prompt: Sort each reader into the register you would ask the AI for.

items.text: A letter to the Permanent Secretary
items.feedback: Permanent secretaries get the official register: full phrases, no contractions.

items.text: A note to a busy colleague who only needs the decision
items.feedback: Busy colleagues get concise: short sentences with the ask up front.

items.text: A message to parents about a school trip
items.feedback: Parents and community members get warm: greetings and human phrasing.

items.text: A thank-you message to a loyal customer
items.feedback: Customers get warm language, such as 'we appreciate…'.

missions.hint: Official for authority, concise for colleagues, warm for customers and community.
missions.support: Think about how you would speak to each person face to face: formally to a Permanent Secretary, briefly to a colleague at their desk, kindly to a parent.
missions.explain: Same content, different register. One extra line, such as 'Rewrite this in a more official tone, keeping the structure', changes the tone without breaking your format.

advanced.title: Advanced: audit a format-following prompt
advanced.scenario: A colleague's prompt reads: 'Here is an old memo and my new notes. Write the new memo.' The AI copied the old memo's dates and a staff name into the new one.
advanced.prompt: Which instructions from today's prompt would have prevented this? Select all that apply.

options.text: Follow the old example's exact structure, but use only the new content.
options.feedback: Yes. This separates the format from the old content.

options.text: Do not copy information from the old example.
options.feedback: Yes. This directly stops old dates and names from leaking into the new memo.
Yes. It stops the AI filling gaps with details that sound right but are made up.

options.text: Make it longer and more detailed.
options.feedback: No. Length has nothing to do with copied details, and a longer memo may contain more invented ones.
No. That changes the house style and does nothing about the copied information.

advanced.hint: The problem was old content leaking in. Which lines keep format and content apart?
advanced.support: The old memo should provide the shape only. Look for instructions that say: structure from the old memo, facts only from the new notes.
advanced.explain: The full prompt tells the AI to copy the structure but not the content, and never to invent anything. Those three lines make the old example safe to use.
